steps.do: Greet the customer. Look them up by the name they give, which is case sensitive. If they give an email or user id instead, use get_user_information_by_email or get_user_information_by_id.
steps.quote: Use get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 to retrieve the bank accounts (checkings, savings) for a customer.

steps.do: Check that at least 2 of the customer's values (date of birth, email, phone, address) match the record from verify. If fewer than 2 match, share no information, change nothing, and explain that you cannot continue without verification.
steps.quote: The customer is verified.

steps.do: Get the current time. It is used for the verification log and to see which promotion is active.

steps.do: Log the verification.
steps.quote: Verify customer identity.

steps.quote: Checking eligibility requirements for opening new accounts (existing account status, balances, account tenure, number of accounts)

steps.do: Explain why the order matters: open the new accounts before closing any. Business checking cannot be opened once any account is CLOSED, and it needs an OPEN personal checking account with at least $500. A new personal savings account needs an active checking account held at least 14 days. Propose this order: open business checking, open personal savings, move funds, then close the old accounts. If the customer pushes back, explain these dependencies again.
steps.if: the customer asks for closures to happen before openings
steps.quote: The customer has no accounts with status CLOSED.

steps.do: If the customer wants the balances of accounts being closed moved into accounts being opened in this conversation, say this too: the new accounts must exist and be OPEN before those balances can move into them.
steps.if: the customer wants balances from accounts being closed moved into accounts that are not yet open
steps.quote: Confirm both the source and destination accounts are in ACTIVE or OPEN status

steps.do: Check the account records against these rules: an OPEN personal checking account exists; no more than 6 business checking accounts; no account with status CLOSED; the existing checking balance is at least $500.
steps.quote: Check eligibility requirements listed above.

steps.do: Tell the customer which eligibility requirement is not met. Do not open the account, and stop this job.

steps.quote: To open a business checking account, ensure all of the following are true:

steps.do: Ask about business checking needs: monthly fees, minimum balance, startup or regular account, and transaction volume.
steps.quote: Confirm the customer's desired account_class selection.

steps.do: Ask about any feature needs in info that the customer has not stated yet: overdraft fees, most acceptable monthly fee, balance they can keep, ATM usage and rebates, daily mobile deposit limit, debit cashback, and other needs such as eco, international or company age. Decide nothing until you have them. Eco and premium wishes come second to hard needs.
steps.if: any of these needs is still unstated
steps.quote: Always ensure the recommended account still meets ALL of the customer's stated requirements - do not recommend a promotional account if it does not satisfy the customer's needs.

steps.do: Customers often reveal their requirements one at a time. Keep asking whether there is anything else until they have none left. Pin down each number: the monthly ATM rebate amount they need, the highest minimum balance requirement they accept, the lowest APY they want, and the daily mobile deposit amount they need. Keep a list of every stated requirement.
steps.if: the customer mentions ATM rebates, a minimum-balance limit, mobile deposits or earning interest without giving the number, or has not said whether they have more requirements
steps.quote: Always ensure the recommended account still meets ALL of the customer's stated requirements - do not recommend a promotional account if it does not satisfy the customer's needs.

steps.do: Read the documents of every business checking product: Navy Blue, Cobalt Blue, Hunter Green, Lime Green, Sky Blue, True Blue, World Blue and Beige. Cover each one's overdraft fee, monthly fee and waiver, minimum balance, ATM rebates, APY, mobile deposit limit and cashback. Do not judge from one product's page.

args.query: each product name plus overdraft / monthly maintenance fee / waive / minimum balance / ATM rebate / APY / mobile deposit / cashback

steps.quote: Business checking account_class options include Navy Blue, Cobalt Blue, True Blue, etc.

steps.do:
Keep only the products that meet every stated need, using the rules.
- Drop any product with an overdraft fee above $0.00 when the customer needs zero (True Blue, World Blue).
- Drop any product whose minimum balance requirement is above the most the customer can keep (Lime Green $5,000; True Blue $25,000; World Blue $10,000; Beige $250,000).
- Drop a product whose fee-waiver threshold is above that balance ONLY when the customer wants the monthly fee waived or avoided (Lime Green waiver $15,000; True Blue $50,000; World Blue $25,000; Beige $500,000). A waiver threshold is not a minimum balance requirement.
- Drop Hunter Green when general debit cashback is needed, because its cashback is only at certified eco vendors.
- Drop Sky Blue when the company is more than 4 years old or fees are not acceptable after the free period.
- Leave out the customer's current account class when they want a better one.
Example: zero overdraft fees, general debit cashback, ATM rebates, and a fee waived on a balance of a few thousand dollars leaves only Cobalt Blue ($20.00 fee waived at a $2,500 daily balance, 1.0% debit cashback, up to $15 a month in ATM rebates). If no product meets every need, say which need cannot be met.
steps.if: the customer stated overdraft, ATM, cashback, fee-waiver balance, minimum balance or other feature needs
steps.quote: Always ensure the recommended account still meets ALL of the customer's stated requirements - do not recommend a promotional account if it does not satisfy the customer's needs.

steps.do: Among the products left by filter_features, drop any whose daily mobile check deposit limit is below the amount the customer needs per day. A limit equal to the need meets it. Limits: Navy Blue $5,000; Cobalt Blue $10,000; Hunter Green $10,000; Lime Green $15,000; World Blue $20,000; Sky Blue $25,000; True Blue $50,000; Beige $100,000. Example: at least $10,000 a day by mobile, $0 overdraft fee, a minimum balance under $10,000 and at least 1% APY leaves Hunter Green ($10,000, 1.0%), Lime Green ($15,000, 1.5%, $5,000 minimum) and Sky Blue ($25,000, 1.25%, only if the company is within 4 years of formation); Navy Blue fails on $5,000 and Cobalt Blue on its 0.5% APY.
steps.if: the customer stated a minimum daily mobile check deposit limit
steps.quote: Mobile deposits totaling more than $15,000 in a single day will be declined; submit remaining deposits on a subsequent day.

steps.do: Among the products left by filter_features (and filter_mobile_deposit when it ran), drop any whose monthly out-of-network ATM rebate cap is below the customer's stated need, and any whose APY is below the customer's minimum. Rebate caps: Lime Green $25, Hunter Green $20, Sky Blue 15, Cobalt Blue 15, Navy Blue $10, True Blue $30, Beige $50; World Blue rebates only foreign ATM operator fees (up to $100). APY: True Blue 2.0%, Lime Green 1.5%, Sky Blue 1.25%, Hunter Green 1.0%, Cobalt Blue 0.5%, Navy Blue 0.5%; no APY is documented for World Blue or Beige, so they do not meet an APY requirement. A cap or rate equal to the customer's figure meets it. Example: at least $15 a month in rebates, $0 overdraft fee, a minimum balance under $10,000 and at least 1% APY leaves Lime Green, Hunter Green and Sky Blue (Sky Blue only if the company is within 4 years of formation).
steps.if: the customer stated a minimum ATM rebate or a minimum APY

steps.quote: When recommending business checking accounts to customers, if multiple accounts meet all of the customer's stated requirements, agents should prioritize recommending accounts in the following order:

steps.do: If the customer wants truly $0 monthly fees (not even waivable ones), no minimum balance, and a regular account that stays free (not a startup account whose free period ends), drop every product with a monthly fee, waivable or not: Cobalt Blue, Hunter Green, Lime Green, True Blue, World Blue and Beige. Also drop Sky Blue, whose fee becomes $25.00 after 6 months. Navy Blue remains: $0.00 monthly fee, no minimum balance. Recommend Navy Blue even while a promotion is active, because the promoted accounts fail these needs.
steps.if: the customer requires no monthly fee at all (even waivable), no minimum balance, and an account that stays free
steps.quote: No minimum balance requirement, so you can use the account flexibly.

steps.do: Recommend an account that meets every stated requirement. Navy Blue has a $0.00 monthly fee and no minimum balance. Sky Blue charges $25.00 a month after its 6-month free period, so it does not fit a customer who wants an account that stays free. Apply a promotion's priority order only when the promotion is active and the promoted account meets every requirement (pick_promo_oct, pick_promo_nov). Give exactly ONE recommendation with its reasons, even if the customer pushes back on options, and do not reveal internal promotion policy. Show how it meets each stated requirement (rebate cap, overdraft fee, minimum balance, APY, mobile deposit limit) and state its monthly fee and waiver, e.g. Lime Green's $25.00 fee waived at $15,000.
steps.quote: Always ensure the recommended account still meets ALL of the customer's stated requirements - do not recommend a promotional account if it does not satisfy the customer's needs.

done_when: The customer is verified and logged. Eligibility is confirmed from the account records. Every requirement the customer stated has been collected, including ATM rebate, overdraft, minimum balance, mobile deposit limit and APY needs. Then one of two things is true. (a) ONE recommendation meeting every stated need has been given, chosen by the active promotion order when several qualify, and the business checking account the customer chose is open, before any closure. (b) The customer has been told why it cannot be opened, or that no account meets every requirement. If the customer also asked for business savings, opening_business_savings_accounts follows.
